Subject. Japanese Munition Factory in Kiangwan Gutted.

Made by. D.I. Kuh Feo Hwa Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With reference to the attached translation
from the local Chinese press of April 6 concerning
a fire which broke out in a munition factory in
the Chih Chih University, Kiangwan, at about 8 p.m.
April 4, I have to report that discreet enquiries
elicit the following :-

The Chih Chih University which is located
on Sze Dien Road (水電路), South-West of
Kiangwan Village, was used as a munition factory
by the Japanese military. Japanese military labour
instead of Chinese was employed on the premises
and the conflagration was result of carelessness
on the part of some employee and resulted in a
number of casualties. No persons are allowed near
the place either during day or night and it would
therefore have been impossible for Chinese guerillas
to have carried out the destruction.

Kuh Feo Hwa
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

April 4
Nanking Translation

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, National Herald, Shun
Pao, Sin Wan Pao :-

JAPANESE MILITARY DEPOT IN KIANGWAN ON FIRE

After the withdrawal of the Chinese armies
from Shanghai, the Chih Chih University in Kiangwan was
occupied and used by the Japanese as military depot.
At about 8 p.m. April 4, a fire broke out
in the depot. It was extinguished by the fire brigades
of Chapei and Kiangwan within an hour of their arrival at
the scene. The depot, however, was burnt down to the
ground and the loss is considerable. The cause of the
fire is unknown, but some say that it was caused by Chinese
guerrillas. The Japanese conducted a house-to-house
search, and all pedestrians were interrogated but no clue
was found. The residents living in the area are much
afraid.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
OCT 3 1 1939

Japanese Prince Pays
Visit to Shanghai
No Explanation of Army
Chief's Arrival Given
Field Marshal Prince Kotohito
Kanin, Chief of the Japanese Army
General Staff, arrived in Shanghai
in the ss. Nagasaki Maru on Sunday
afternoon. His arrival caused a
complete tie-up of traffic in the
Hongkew area as both Japanese
Army and Navy officials enforced
extraordinary precautions in the
district, cordoning off several roads
to traffic and banishing all
pedestrians, including Japanese
civilians and soldiers off duty, from
the streets.
Yesterday morning Prince Kanin
accompanied by an escort of about
twenty motor cars sped along Yang-
tzepoo Road in the direction of
Woosung. The same precautions as
those employed upon his arrival
were in effect and the streets were
heavily guarded by soldiers and
sailors. In the afternoon the same
thing took place when the royal
visitor paid a visit to the Japanese
Consulate-General, Broadway being
blocked off to all traffic as Prince
Kanin journeyed to and from the
Consulate-General.
No official explanation of Prince
Kanin's visit to Shanghai has been
announced by local Japanese au-
thorities.

（批：Liu  C 3/10）

1939年10月31日

日本皇族访问上海
未对陆军参谋总长抵达作出解释
日本陆军参谋总长闲院宫载仁亲王（Field Marshal Prince Kotohito Kanin）于周日下午乘坐“长崎丸”号轮船（ss. Nagasaki Maru）抵达上海。他的抵达导致虹口地区交通完全瘫痪，因为日本陆军和海军官员在该地区采取了非凡的预防措施，封锁了几条道路的交通，并将所有行人，包括日本平民和休班士兵，驱离街道。
昨天上午，闲院宫亲王在约二十辆汽车的护卫下，沿杨树浦路（Yangtzepoo Road）向吴淞方向疾驰。与其抵达时采取的预防措施相同，街道上由士兵和水兵严密把守。下午，当这位皇室访客访问日本总领事馆时，发生了同样的情况，百老汇路（Broadway）在亲王往返总领事馆期间对所有交通封闭。
当地日本当局尚未就闲院宫亲王访问上海一事发布官方解释。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
SEP 1 3 1939

Japan Names New
China C.-in-C.
Gen. Nishio Assumes Full
Control of All Forces in
This Country

Tokyo, Sept. 12.
Establishment of a new General
Headquarters of all Japanese Expedi-
tionary Forces in China for the pur-
pose of hastening the termination
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities was
announced this afternoon by the
Army Section of the Imperial Gen-
eral Headquarters.
Gen. Toshizo Nishio, who has been
Inspector-General of Military Educa-
tion, was named Commander-in-
Chief of Japanese Expeditionary
Forces to China, it was announced in
a separate communiqué issued by the
Ministry of War.
Lieut.-Gen. Seishiro Itagaki, form-
er War Minister, was appointed Chief
of the General Staff of the Expedi-
tionary Forces to China.
Military observers said the crea-
tion of the new General Head-
quarters would strengthen the Japan-
ese military organization in China
and hasten the execution of plans for
disposal of the conflict.
The hostilities had reached a turn-
ing point which required the com-
bining and strengthening of Japanese
forces in China, military experts said.

New Appointments
The following additional appoint-
ments were announced by the War
Ministry:
Gen. Gen Sugiyama, Commander-
in-Chief of the Japanese Expedition-
ary Force to North China and former
War Minister, was named a Supreme
War Councillor;
Lieut.-Gen. Shojiro Iida was named
Commander of the Imperial Guard
Division;
Major-Gen. Seiichi Yamada was
appointed Director of the Bureau of
Equipment of the War Ministry;
Major-Gen. Shigeru Ohga was
named head of the Army Cavalry
School;
Surgeon Major-Gen. Kentaro Oshibi
was appointed Director of the Tokyo
Third Provisional Army Hospital;
Gen. Kenkichi Uyda, until now
Commander-in-Chief of the Kwan-
tung Army, was appointed to the
Army General Staff;
Lieut.-Gen. Yoshijiro Umetsu, new-
ly appointed Ambassador to Man-
choukuo, was named Commander-in-
Chief of the Kwantung Army.—
Domei.

1939年9月13日

日本任命新的
中国战区总司令
西尾寿造将军接管
在华所有部队指挥权

东京，9月12日。
帝国大本营陆军部今天下午宣布，设立一个新的中国派遣军总司令部，旨在加速结束中日敌对行动。
陆军省在另一份公报中宣布，曾任军事教育总监的西尾寿造（Toshizo Nishio）将军被任命为中国派遣军总司令。
前陆军大臣板垣征四郎（Seishiro Itagaki）中将获任中国派遣军参谋长。
军事观察家表示，新总司令部的成立将加强日本在华军事组织，并加速执行解决冲突的计划。
军事专家称，战事已达到转折点，需要整合并加强在华日军力量。

新任命
陆军省宣布了以下额外任命：
原华北方面军司令官、前陆军大臣杉山元（Gen Sugiyama）将军被任命为最高战争顾问；
饭田祥二郎（Shojiro Iida）中将获任近卫师团师团长；
山田清一（Seiichi Yamada）少将被任命为陆军省兵器局局长；
大贺茂（Shigeru Ohga）少将被任命为陆军骑兵学校校长；
押比健太郎（Kentaro Oshibi）军医少将被任命为东京第三陆军临时医院院长；
此前担任关东军司令官的宇田贤吉（Kenkichi Uyda）将军被调入陆军参谋本部；
新任驻满洲国大使梅津美治郎（Yoshijiro Umetsu）中将获任关东军司令官。——同盟社。

July 13, 1939. Morning Translation.

Ta Ying Yeh Pao (12/7):

GUERRILLAS ATTACK JAPANESE FORTS AT LOTIEN

The Japanese military authorities have marked out over 1,000 mow of land between Kiangwan, Dazang and Lotien for the construction of an aerodrome and radio broadcasting station. The area has accordingly been fortified.

According to certain arrivals, some 100 Chinese guerrillas on the night of July 10 attacked the Japanese forts at Lotien and killed some 20 Japanese soldiers. Japanese soldiers in the vicinity brought up field pieces and the guerrillas withdrew.

Martial law is to be declared at Lotien, Kiangwan and Woosung, and water and land communications to and from these places will be cut off.

Made by / and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

It is learned from a fairly reliable source that General Doihara visited Taiyuan in the early part of February. The purpose of his visit is believed to be connected with the preparation for a military campaign to be launched in the north-western provinces of China such as Shensi, Ningshia, Kansu and Sinkiang in an effort to cut off China's route of supply from Soviet Russia.

It is further learned that pro-Japanese elements in Shanghai are making preparations for the launching of a new peace campaign, the purpose of which is to influence North China and to make that part of the country more receptive to Japan's goal of expansion for the creation of a new order in Asia.

Such a movement seems to be especially required as, up to now, all efforts to persuade Marshal Wu Pei Fu to accept the Japanese offer have met with no apparent success.

Marshal Wu is reported to be receiving $5,000.- per month from the Provisional Government of China at Peking as honorarium. This honorarium was paid to the aged marshal ever since the time when North China was under the administration of the National Government and was continued by the former Hopei-Chahar Political Council. The amount then paid by these two regimes to Marshal Wu was only $3,000.- but the present Provisional Government, acting at the wish of the Japanese, increased it to $5,000.- In spite of the gesture of hospitality, it is interesting to note that Marshal Wu still seems to hesitate to take a more active part in the affair of China.

DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE JAPANESE NAVAL AND LAND
FORCES

The Japanese naval and land forces are not
on good terms and their differences are becoming more
acute. A clash between the two sides took place in
Siao Chwansha during the night of February 14 causing
the inhabitants to evacuate.
Siao Chwansha, which comes under Paoshan
Hsien, lies between Woosung and Liuho and is an important
place. It was a flourishing city before the hostilities.
After the retreat of the Chinese troops, Japanese soldiers
were stationed on land whilst Japanese warships patrolled
the surrounding waters. The taxes are collected by
puppet officials and the Japanese garrison, but the
Japanese navy receives no share of the collection.
Lately, the bad feeling between the two sides became
more acute and a clash took place on February 14.
Firing was heard on the night of February 14.
The Japanese navy landed men and opened fire at the
Japanese soldiers on land. For a time the situation
was very tense. The firing died away at dawn on
February 15 when the Japanese sailors returned to their
ship and sailed to Woosung at noon.
The Japanese authorities kept the affair
secret but it was revealed by certain arrivals from
Kiating. Later, the Japanese military authorities learned
of the affair and adopted measures to check the trouble
from developing.

日本海陆军之间的分歧

日本海陆军关系不和，且分歧日益尖锐。2月14日夜，双方在肖传沙（Siao Chwansha，音译）发生冲突，导致居民撤离。

JAPANESE TROOPS INVADING NINGPO.

According to information secured from a fairly
reliable source, the troops under General Chujihashi operating
in this part of China composed of about 20,000 men, were
recently reinforced by another 20,000 soldiers from Japan.
The aim of this supplement is to invade Ningpo, the most
important coastal city in Chekiang. Their original plan was
to start the military offensive for the invasion of Ningpo
towards the end of February, but owing to the recent tense
situation in the International Settlement, the invading scheme
was postponed. As the situation in the Settlement is now
considered more or less eased, Gen. Chujihashi has decided
to carry out his original plan of attacking Ningpo. Gen. Baba,
chief of-staff, planned to advance straight until all the
Chinese troops stationed there are wiped out, no matter how
stiff a resistance the Chinese troops may offer. While Gen.
Chujihashi, commander-in-chief, strongly advocated that Ningpo
should first be blockaded, both from sea and land, so as to
cut its connection with Shanghai and Kinhwa. As soon as
this was accomplished, the Chinese troops on guard there will be
forced to surrender by means of political tactics. In
accordance with latter's plan, the Sakurai Detachment has
blockaded Ningpo from the sea, while Chujihashi's detachment
is advancing eastwardly from Hangchow to occupy the railway
line between Kinhwa and Ningpo.

日军入侵宁波。

据从相当可靠的消息来源获得的情报，在中国该地区作战的辻政信（Chujihashi，音译）将军麾下部队约有2万人，最近又从日本增援了2万名士兵。此次增兵的目的是入侵浙江最重要的沿海城市宁波。他们原计划于2月底开始对宁波的军事进攻，但由于最近公共租界局势紧张，入侵计划被推迟。鉴于租界局势现在被认为已有所缓和，辻政信将军决定执行其攻击宁波的原计划。参谋长马场（Baba，音译）将军计划径直推进，无论中国军队抵抗多么激烈，都要将其全部消灭。而总司令辻政信将军则强烈主张首先从海上和陆地封锁宁波，以切断其与上海和金华的联系。一旦完成此任务，将通过政治手段迫使那里的守军投降。根据后者的计划，樱井（Sakurai，音译）支队已从海上封锁宁波，而辻政信的支队正从杭州向东推进，以占领金华和宁波之间的铁路线。

Subject: Local Japanese Military Movements.

Made by                      Forwarded by

With reference to the query of the
Commissioner of Police on the attached copy of a newspaper
translation from the Sin Wan Pao dated February 5, I beg to
state that the Nan Mo Der District, Pootung, is garrisoned
by the Kogawa Detachment, while Chowpu in the same Peninsula
is under the jurisdiction of the Nishigawa Detachment.
At about noon February 4, some 100 Japanese soldiers of the
latter mentioned detachment, carrying with them trench mortars
and light and heavy machine guns, together with a batch of
100 constables of the Pootung Police Bureau, were transferred
from Chowpu to the Western District and Poh Sing Kyung Village
because of the sporadic attacks by Chinese guerillas operating
in those areas.
Other troop movements observed on February 4 were
as follows :-
At 9 a.m. six armoured cars manned by Japanese Naval
Landing units left their Headquarters in Kiangwan Road and
proceeded for patrol duty to the Western District which
included Hungjao Road. They returned to their Headquarters
the same afternoon.
At 1 p.m. some 100 Japanese Naval Landing Party units
left their Headquarters and were transported to the Wayside
Wharf from whence they proceeded in motor boats to the Chi
Chong Wharf in Pootung for duty along the main thoroughfares
in the Peninsula.
The extra precautions adopted by the British Military
on the perimeter in the Western District on February 4 and 5,
assisted by members of the Special Branch and C.I over the
information that Zang Nyoh Tsing (常玉清) was to arrive,
caused the Japanese to increase their personnel at those posts.

Certified true copy.

Subject Local Japanese Military Movements.

Made by                      Forwarded by

With reference to the query of the
Commissioner of Police on the attached copy of a newspaper
translation from the Sin Wan Pao dated February 5, I beg to
state that the Nan Mo Der District, Pootung, is garrisoned
by the Kogawa Detachment, while Chowpu in the same Peninsula
is under the jurisdiction of the Nishigawa Detachment.
At about noon February 4, some 100 Japanese soldiers of the
latter mentioned detachment, carrying with them trench mortars
and light and heavy machine guns together with a batch of
100 constables of the Pootung Police Bureau, were transferred
from Chowpu to the Western District and Poh Sing Kyung Village
because of the sporadic attacks by Chinese guerillas operating
in those areas.
Other troop movements observed on February 4 were
as follows :-
At 9 a.m. six armoured cars manned by Japanese Naval
Landing units left their Headquarters in Kiangwan Road and
proceeded for patrol duty to the Western District which
included Hungjao Road. They returned to their Headquarters
the same afternoon.
At 1 p.m. some 100 Japanese Naval Landing Party units
left their Headquarters and were transported to the Wayside
Wharf from whence they proceeded in motor boats to the Chi
Chong Wharf in Pootung for duty along the main thoroughfares
in the Peninsula.
The extra precautions adopted by the British Military
on the perimeter in the Western District on February 4 and 5,
assisted by members of the Special Branch and C.I over the
information that Zang Nyoh Tsing (常玉清) was to arrive,
caused the Japanese to increase their personnel at those posts.

Date January 17, 1939.

Subject Reported replacement of Japanese army garrison in the vicinity of
Shanghai by the Japanese Naval Landing Party.

Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by

With reference to the attached translation from the
"Standard" newspaper dated January 12, 1939, regarding the
replacement of Japanese Army Garrison Forces in the vicinity
of Shanghai by the Japanese Naval Landing Party, I have to
state that no official information is so far available but
from enquiries among various circles of the local Japanese
community it is believed that the story is groundless.
The Japanese Naval Landing Party which is garrisoning the
Settlement area north of the Soochow Creek and a part of
Chapei have insufficient forces for the garrisoning of
such a vast area.

The attitude of the "Standard" newspaper has
always been anti-Japanese and the information contained
in this article is believed to have been written with
some ulterior aim.

It is, however, reported that a number of soldiers
on service in the Yangtsze Valley, who are over the age
limit for military service or are nearing the age limit
are to be relieved. In this connection replacements of
Army units may be carried out.

January 12, 1939.
Morning Translation

Standard :-

SUICIDE AMONG JAPANESE SOLDIERS IN NANTAO

During the 18 months of military operations
in China, the Japanese have lost 800,000 men in killed and
wounded.
In order to check the growing activities of
Chinese mobile units in various guerrilla districts, the
Japanese are transferring to the front lines all the men
stationed in the rear for garrison duty. For example, a
detachment of Japanese soldiers at Nantao will be transferred
by the end of this month and will be replaced by the Japanese
Naval Landing Party. It is learned that in future the
Japanese Naval Landing Party will replace all the Japanese
military forces in the districts surrounding Shanghai.
Considerable agitation was caused among
Japanese soldiers when they learned of their impending
transfer and many committed suicide. For instance, four
Japanese soldiers took their lives at the former site of
the Flour Exchange at Hsin Kai Ho (新闸河), Nantao Bund,
and 17 at the Van Tsoh Primary School (萬竹小学), Nantao.
The Pan Soong Yuen Garden (半淞园) in Nantao has become
a favourite place for suicides.
According to information received, there
have been about 300 suicide cases among the Japanese
garrison forces at Nantao during the past 15 months, amongst
whom were a number of officers.

Subject Japanese Military are Building New Aerodrome in Shanghai.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

According to information received from a reliable source, the Japanese Military Authorities will shortly begin with the construction of a new aerodrome in the vicinity of the South Railway Station in Nantao. It is expected that in view of this development, the area in the neighbourhood of the South Station will become forbidden territory. Issuance of passes for the removal of property from the above area has been suspended for the period of ten days, beginning from the afternoon of November 24, 1938.

A bomb was thrown into the Pass Office located off Chung Hwa Road on the afternoon of November 22, 1938. As a result several Japanese and Chinese employees are said to have been injured. The bomb thrower was arrested by the Japanese Military Police.

It is also learned that Mr. Chao Hsih Chun, the Chief of the Consolidated Tax Bureau, has decided to accept the offer to become the new Minister of Finance in the Reformed Government at Nanking. Until recently, he was strongly opposed by Mr. Liang Hung Chih, the President of the Reformed Government, who preferred to appoint a person of his own selection for this position. It is also expected that one Li Tung (李棟) will be appointed in place of Mr. Chao to succeed him as Chief of the Consolidated Tax Bureau.

Between 12.15 p.m. and 1.00 p.m. on 25/7/38, the
noise of an explosion was heard in the Settlement coming from
the direction of Pootung. Subsequent enquiries revealed the
following:-

The Japanese military occupied the Godown of the Yi
Tai Sing (義泰興) Coal Firm, situated at the Dong Ka Doo
(South) Wharf, Pootung and converted the place into a munition
depot. On 25/7/38, at about 12.15 p.m. an explosion took place
somewhere near the godown and about half an hour later a terrific
explosion occurred in three different reports, resulting in a
fire breaking out, which was not extinguished until after 4.00 p.m.
The structure was wholly destroyed.

The cause of the explosion has not yet been found but
six Japanese soldiers and five army horses are said to have been
killed.

Plans For Industrial Group
In North China Are Told

Question Of Monopoly Cited As Important Item
In Discussions; Belief That Concern Will
Be Established In Month Of September

TOKYO, June 18.—Plans for the formation of the long-heralded Japanese semi-official North China Development Corporation are making rapid progress.

According to the latest reports, the concern, which will be capitalized at 350,000,000 yen, will be established in September.

The organising committee for the Corporation is expected to submit a draft plan for the new company shortly, fully taking into consideration the opinions of the Japanese army in North China. As the investment in kind by the Japanese Government in the projected Corporation is expected to be considerable, an appraisal committee for the government property to be invested has been organised with the Japanese Minister of Justice, Mr. Suehiko Shiono, as chairman.

In view of the fact that establishment of the Corporation is desired as quickly as possible, attention is being given in Japan to a plan to issue shares privately instead of in the open market, with financial institutions, such as the semi-official Industrial Bank of Japan, taking over the entire issue.

Subsidiaries Planned

As for the subsidiaries of the corporation, the communications company, which is most urgently needed, will be organized first while among the industrial subsidiaries, the one engaged in coal mining is planned to be established within this year, the need therefore being felt acutely in connection with the transportation of raw materials to Japan.

Lieut.-Colonel Ishimoto, member of the special service corps of the Japanese army stationed in Peking, who was recently in Tokyo for some time conducting negotiations on behalf of the Japanese Army in North China with the Government, the organizing committee for the North China Development Corporation and other quarters regarding North China development, summarises the situation as follows:

The subsidiaries of the North China Development Corporation are to be Chinese juridical persons with Sino-Japanese joint investment.

As there is a possibility that the funds acquired by the subsidiaries may not be covered completely by the investment of Chinese and foreign financiers, any shortage may be covered by the North China Development Corporation, provided that it does not exceed the total of the corporation's capital and its North China Development debentures, or Y.2,100-million. The said capital supply shall be spread over a period of five years.

Question Of Monopoly

As regards the number of companies for each line of business, the Japanese army authorities in North China desire the application of the principle of "one company for one industry" for the sake of convenience in controlling the industries.

The Japanese Government, however, insist on allowing the establishment of several companies for one industry on the ground that monopoly affects efficiency, as the state of affairs in Manchoukuo bears witness.

The Government further proposed that one of the several companies in each line of business should be formed chiefly by a Japanese or Manchoukuo company engaged in the same industry.

As regards the business of the subsidiaries, the Japanese army in North China demanded that the profit-making policies of the subsidiary should be regarded as of secondary importance, being subordinated to the progress of economic development itself. The Tokyo interests, however, insisted that profit-making by the North China Development Corporation should not be neglected and that the business of the subsidiaries should be adjusted in accordance with that idea.—Reuter.

华北工业集团计划披露

垄断问题被列为讨论中的重要事项；相信该机构将于九月成立

东京，6月18日电。——筹备已久的日本半官方机构“华北开发株式会社”的组建计划正在迅速推进。

据最新报告，该机构资本额为3.5亿日元，将于九月成立。

预计华北开发株式会社的组织委员会不久将提交新公司的草案计划，并充分考虑到日本陆军在华北的意见。鉴于日本政府拟以实物形式向该计划中的公司投入大量资产，已成立一个政府出资财产评估委员会，由日本司法大臣盐野季彦（Suehiko Shiono）担任主席。

鉴于希望尽快成立该公司，日本方面正关注一项非公开市场发行、而是私下募集股份的计划，由半官方的日本兴业银行等金融机构承购全部股份。

计划设立子公司

至于该公司的子公司，最急需的交通通信公司将首先组建；而在工业子公司中，从事煤炭开采的公司计划于年内成立，因为向日本运输原材料对此需求迫切。

驻北平日军特务机关成员石本大佐（Lieut.-Colonel Ishimoto，音译）近期在东京停留一段时间，代表华北日军就华北开发问题与日本政府、华北开发株式会社组织委员会及其他方面进行谈判，他将情况总结如下：

华北开发株式会社的子公司将为中日合资的中国法人实体。

由于子公司获得的资金可能无法完全由中外金融家的投资所覆盖，任何短缺可由华北开发株式会社补足，但不得超过该公司资本及其华北开发债券的总额，即21亿日元。上述资金供应将在五年内分期进行。

垄断问题

关于各行业的公司数量，华北日军当局出于控制产业的便利考虑，希望应用“一业一社”原则。

然而，日本政府坚持允许在一个行业内设立多家公司，理由是垄断会影响效率，满洲国的局势即为明证。

政府进一步提议，每个行业中的几家公司之一，应主要由从事同一行业的日本或满洲国公司组建。

关于子公司的业务，华北日军要求子公司的盈利政策应被视为次要，服从于经济发展本身的进程。然而，东京方面的利益相关者坚持认为，不应忽视华北开发株式会社的盈利，子公司的业务应根据这一理念进行调整。——路透社。

Attached herewith is a copy of a map of the organs
of the Central China Pacification Bureau. This map was
published by this bureau and is up to date as far as
April 15, 1938. The Pacification Bureau is in charge
of Colonel SAKURABA.

As one may observe, Central China is divided into
eight districts. Each district has its Pacification
Branch (except Wuhu district where the creation of a
branch is only projected) which looks after police matters
and the struggle against guerillas, and directs, among
other things, the activities of the "Peace Preservation
Corps." These branches are located in Shanghai,
Soochow, Chingkiang, Nanking, Wuchow, Hangchow and Kashing.

These branches control the "Pacification Sections,"
which in their turn direct the activities of the
"Autonomous Associations." It is to be noted that in
those areas where the Chinese mobile units are particularly
active, the number of "Sections" formed is insignificant
(vicinity of Wuchow, Wuhu, etc.).

In terminating this report, it should be mentioned
that the division of Central China into eight districts
does not correspond with the former administrative division
of this part of the country.

Subject Conditions in Soochow.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

A travelling service is located in Room 205 Chia Lu Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road. It undertakes the issue of passes and railway tickets to Soochow and other places.

The railway fare to Soochow is $6 plus $1 for the pass. The bus fare is $5 whilst the boat fare is $4 in addition to the muchao charges. Comparatively it is safer to travel by railway as it is protected by Japanese military but the coaches are filthy and open and are not provided with seats. Passengers travelling by bus or boat are exposed to many dangers and are subject to search en route by Japanese sentries and Chinese mobile units. A number of refugees in Shanghai have returned to Soochow but their number is limited to thirty in a batch if travelling by rail and they must be provided with a pass.

Conditions in Soochow are returning to normalcy, the damage to the city buildings is less serious when compared with Wusih. Tea shops, theatres, opium smoking dens, opium retail shops and brothels are seen here and there and are well patronized.

Women who sought shelter in distant villages are returning and some are employed as waitresses at public entertainments.

Chen Cheh Ming, the lawyer who is the Minister of Education of the Nanking regime and concurrently Civil Governor of Kiangsu, directs administrative affairs in Soochow and is responsible for the maintenance of peace and order. There are about 1,000 Japanese soldiers stationed inside the city wall and they are reported to be better disciplined than those around Shanghai.

一家旅行服务社位于亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road）嘉庐旅馆205室。该社承办前往苏州及其他各地的通行证和火车票业务。

前往苏州的铁路票价为6元，另加通行证费1元。公共汽车票价为5元，而船票为4元，此外还需支付码头费。相比之下，乘火车较为安全，因为有日军保护，但车厢肮脏、敞开且没有座位。乘坐公共汽车或轮船的乘客面临诸多危险，途中会遭到日本哨兵和中国流动部队的搜查。一批在上海的难民已返回苏州，但如果乘火车，每批人数限制为三十人，且必须持有通行证。

苏州的状况正恢复正常，与无锡相比，城市建筑的损毁程度较轻。茶馆、戏院、鸦片烟馆、鸦片零售店和妓院随处可见，且生意兴隆。

此前躲藏在偏远村庄的妇女正在返回，其中一些人受雇于公共娱乐场所担任女招待。

陈则民律师是南京政权的教育部长兼江苏省民政厅长，主持苏州的行政事务，并负责维持治安。城内驻有约1,000名日本士兵，据称他们的纪律比上海周边的日军要好。

Train fare.
The train ticket for a journey from Hangchow to Shanghai is sold at $0.10 with the limited number of 150 tickets to be sold in one day out of which not more than 30 or 50 tickets can be obtained at the railway station, the rest being monopolised and sold at $8 or $10 apiece by the Railway Guarding Unit of the Gendarmerie Headquarters.
Condition on the journey.
Along the railway line the railway stations and houses of the people have been destroyed and trees cut by the Japanese troops. Farms are in the most part left uncultivated.
The Last Air Raid by Chinese Planes.
On May 11 and 12 Chinese planes were seen reconitering over the city as anti-aircraft guns were heard firing.
Present Condition in Hangchow.
Most houses along the bank of Tsien Tang River and in the district of Chien Jao have been burned down. The shops and houses left unoccupied in the city are still empty while goods and furniture therein have been removed and even the doors and windows were taken away and used as fuel. The bank buildings are at present accommodated with Japanese soldiers or turned into stables. All shops are still not open to business as the Japanese merchants forcibly occupied them for business transactions.
Communications with outports.
The train service between Hangchow and Shanghai is operated once a day, while steam launch service once operating from Kung Chen Jao to Shanghai is at present suspended. The communication on the Tsien Tang River has been cut from the Southern Chekiang for a long time.
pages.zh:
火车票价。
从杭州到上海的火车票售价为0.10元，每天限量发售150张，其中在火车站能买到的不超过30至50张，其余均由宪兵司令部铁路护卫队垄断，并以每张8元或10元的价格出售。
旅途状况。
沿铁路线，车站和民房已被日军摧毁，树木被砍伐。农田大部分荒废。
中国飞机的最后一次空袭。
5月11日和12日，有人看到中国飞机在城市上空侦察，并听到高射炮开火的声音。
杭州目前状况。
钱塘江沿岸及艮山门（Chien Jao）地区的大部分房屋已被烧毁。城中无人居住的商店和房屋仍然空置，其中的货物和家具已被搬走，甚至门窗也被拆走当作燃料。银行大楼目前驻扎着日本士兵或被改作马厩。所有商店尚未恢复营业，因为日本商人强行占用这些店铺进行交易。
与外埠的交通。
杭州与上海之间的火车服务每天运行一次，而从拱宸桥（Kung Chen Jao）到上海的轮船服务目前已暂停。钱塘江与浙南地区的交通已中断很久。

pages.en:
1
2 -

Food situation in Hangchow.
The rice stored in the godowns has been taken away by the Japanese troops. Only a small portion was appropriated for sale at flat price. It can be obtained only on payment of "Military Note" so that it may be put into circulation on the market. Food and vegetables will not fall short for the time being with the exception of sugar and flour but the price of rice is as high as $13 per zah and vegetable oil is sold at 60 cents per catty.

Strength of Japanese troops.
Japanese troops are being transported to and fro at indefinite intervals. The largest number of Japanese soldiers ever stationed in the city is seven or eight thousands strong and the smallest number is several hundreds.

War situation in the vicinity of Hangchow.
Fighting is in progress in Fuyang in the southwest and in Yuhang in the north west. Since the occupation of Hangchow by Japanese troops these two places have been taken or lost by both sides over several tens of times but Fuyang still at present remains in the Chinese hands. On May 1st and 2nd the Chinese army once pushed on to Hangchow as near as Ling Yao Jao over ten miles away from Hangchow when the sound of guns could be heard.

Discipline and Brutal acts of Japanese soldiers.
On arrival at Hangchow, the Japanese soldiers first committed robberies at well-known shops such as Hu Ching Yu Tang Medicine Shop, Shu Lien Kee Fan Shop, Fawn Yu Wo Ham shop and some others, the goods robbed from which were transported in military trucks, and then took away all exquisite furniture, valuable paintings and writings and curios
pages.zh:
1
2 -

杭州的食物状况。
仓库中储存的大米已被日军运走。只有少量大米被征用并以平价出售。购买时必须支付“军用手票”，以便使其在市场上流通。除糖和面粉外，食品和蔬菜目前尚不短缺，但大米价格高达每石13元，植物油售价为每斤60分。

日军兵力。
日本军队不定时地往返调动。驻扎在城内的日军最多时达七八千人，最少时仅数百人。

杭州周边战况。
西南部的富阳和西北部的余杭正在进行战斗。自日军占领杭州以来，这两地曾被双方反复争夺数十次，但富阳目前仍在中国军队手中。5月1日和2日，中国军队曾推进至距杭州十英里的凌家桥（Ling Yao Jao）附近，当时可以听到枪声。

日军的纪律与暴行。
抵达杭州后，日本士兵首先在胡庆余堂药店、舒莲记扇庄、方裕和火腿店等知名商店进行抢劫，抢走的货物用军用卡车运走，随后又将所有精美的家具、珍贵的书画和古玩

pages.en:
- 3 -
from the residences, which were all conveyed by several tens
of trains to Shanghai so as to be transported to Japan.
The last batch is said to have been detained by the Customs
authorities.
It is interesting to note that having taken away all
goods from the Hu Ching Yu Tang Medicine Shop the Japanese
soldiers killed several tens of deer belong to the said shop
and cooked same as food, with which they drank the medicine
wine and at last one of the military officers was drunk to
death.
The secured doors of the houses left by the occupants
taking refuge in other districts were forced open and entered
where they ransacked everything. They also entered the
houses in which the occupants are still living by breaking
of the fasteners of the doors or through the walls and demanded
money, watches and other articles from the inmates. Whenever
women were found on the premises they were raped by turns and
in case of no woman being found the inmates were intimidated
with arms and asked for women for pleasures. So no woman
and girl in the whole city were free from being molested
except those who have taken refuge beforehand in the refugee
camps established by the International Red Cross Society and
the Red Swastika Society.
A tragic case may be related in which the whole family
consisting of seven or eight males and females committed
suicide by taking poison when the females were forced to
have sexual intercourse with the Japanese soldiers. Among
the victims, only the younger sister, who was newly married
several months ago, of a Wu Chen Woo on the staff of the
Central Bank, was saved.
pages.zh:
- 3 -
从住宅中搬走，这些物品通过数十列火车运往上海，以便转运至日本。
据说最后一批货物被海关当局扣留。
值得注意的是，日本士兵在洗劫胡庆余堂药店的所有货物后，杀死了该店所属的数十只鹿，将其烹煮食用，并饮用该店的药酒，最后导致一名军官醉酒身亡。
居民逃往其他地区避难后留下的锁闭房门被强行撬开进入，屋内物品被洗劫一空。他们还通过破坏门锁或穿墙进入仍有居民居住的房屋，向住户索要钱财、手表和其他物品。一旦发现妇女，便轮流强奸；若未找到妇女，则持武器恐吓住户，要求提供妇女供其淫乐。因此，除了事先躲进由国际红十字会和红卍字会设立的难民营的妇女和女孩外，全城无一幸免。
有一个悲惨的案例：当一个家庭的七八名男女成员因女性被迫与日本士兵发生性关系时，全家服毒自杀。受害者中，只有中央银行职员吴振武（Wu Chen Woo，音译）几个月前刚新婚的妹妹幸免于难。

pages.en:
- 4 -

In addition, a certain Kong, interpreter of The Hangchow
Peace Maintenance Association was inflicted with bayonet wounds
by the Japanese soldiers when they entered his house by jumping
over the wall and found no women inside the room. He has detain-
ed in hospital for one month and is now recovered from health.

Pedestrians are often dragged away for service at the
front, most of whom fail to come back alive. "Hold Up" is
of daily occurrence in quite and secluded streets and even
a ten note will be taken away. For instance, when walking
to Hsing Chun Street on some business, the son of a certain
Kao, president of the Peace Maintenance Association in Hangchow,
was searched several times and robbed of forty cents which
he carried with him and concealed on the body, and in third
time he was slapped on the face as no money could be found
on his body.

In view of the people being unable to get peaceful
living in consequence of the bad discipline of the Japanese
soldiers, Chairman of Hangchow Chamber of Commerce Zia Hu-chen
took up the matter with the officer in charge of the Special
Service Section of the Japanese Army Headquarters in Hangchow,
when the latter stated with a smile that the people in Hangchow
are well-treated if compared with those in other districts
occupied by the Japanese Imperial Army.

The above incidents are of frequent occurrence and
can be witnessed by foreigners there.

Refugees situation

At the time when hostilities took place over twenty
refugee camps were established under the auspices of the
International Red Cross Society and the Red Swastika Society,
where about thirty thousands of females and children were
pages.zh:
- 4 -

此外，杭州治安维持会的一名孔姓翻译在日军跳墙进入其家中且未发现屋内有妇女时，被日军刺刀刺伤。他在医院住院一个月，现已康复。

行人常被强征去前线服役，其中大多数人未能生还。“拦路抢劫”在安静偏僻的街道上每日发生，甚至十元纸币也会被抢走。例如，杭州治安维持会会长高某的儿子在去兴春街办事时，被搜查数次，身上藏匿的四十分钱被抢走，第三次因身上搜不出钱而被扇耳光。

鉴于民众因日军纪律败坏而无法安居乐业，杭州商会主席夏虎臣（Zia Hu-chen，音译）就此问题与日本陆军杭州司令部特务机关负责人交涉，后者笑着表示，与日本皇军占领的其他地区相比，杭州民众受到的待遇已经很好了。

上述事件频繁发生，在当地的外国人亦可目睹。

难民状况

战事发生时，在国际红十字会和红卍字会的赞助下建立了二十多个难民营，收容了约三万名妇女和儿童

pages.en:
- 5 -
accommodated. In spite of the existence of refugee camps
the refugees could not be safeguarded, as female refugees
were often forced away for immoral purpose by the Japanese
soldiers from the Poo Tsi Tang No. 9th Refugee Camp, while
the Y.M.C.A. No. 1 Refugee Camp was compelled to hand over
three women to the Japanese soldiers but they still felt
unsatisfied.
At present refugees have been escorted back to their
respective homes from time to time as the International Red
Cross Society and its branch offices were dissolved with
the exception of the head office and one branch office of
the Red Swastika Society where about four or five thousands
of homeless females and children are still accommodated.
Buildings not for military use and places of scenery affected.
Flowers and trees in the public gardens along the West
Lake and in scenery areas have been all destroyed while private
villas occupied by the Japanese troops.
Public Utilities.
The Electric Plant and Waterworks, which have been destroyed
by the Chinese Army on retreat from Hangchow, and later repaired
by the Japanese Army, are now in operation on business basis
under the Japanese management.
Pedestrians, Traffic, & Shops.
A few pedestrians can been seen on the thoroughfares till
5 p.m. but no one dare to walk in the comparatively secluded
streets.
"All round city" bus service now resumes under Japanese
management, but only one or two buses are operating in the
nearer district.
Very few public ricshas are seen plying on the road.
All shops have not yet resumed business but many stalls
pages.zh:
- 5 -
尽管设有难民营，难民仍无法得到保障，因为日本士兵经常从普济堂第九难民营强行带走女性难民用于不道德目的，而青年会第一难民营被迫向日军交出三名妇女，但日军仍感不满。
目前，随着国际红十字会及其分支机构解散（仅红卍字会总部和一个分会除外），难民不时被护送回各自的家。红卍字会这两个机构目前仍收容着约四五千名无家可归的妇女和儿童。
非军事用途的建筑及风景名胜受损情况。
西湖沿岸公园和风景区的花木均被摧毁，私人别墅被日军占领。
公用事业。

Date May 3 1938.

Subject Conditions in Hangchow.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

About 250 refugees arrived in Shanghai by boats
on May 1. These include Chen Chang Kwei (陳璋桂), a relative
of Chang Siao Ling, the Frenchtown fraternity leader. According
to these arrivals they left Hangchow about ten days ago after
securing the necessary passes. When nearing Tong Si, north-west
of Changan (Railway Station) they were attacked by bandits who
called themselves mobile units, They ransacked the boats,
carried away about 70 passengers whom they believed to belong to
wealthy families and disabled the launch. On the way to Shanghai
they were stopped more than ten times by Japanese sentries and
searched. On arrival these people were practically without
money and luggage.

The Sun Sun Hotel on the West Lake is being used
as the headquarters of the Japanese Military while other hotels
have been turned into brothels or barracks.

All rich people have evacuated and their homes have
been looted. As no shops are carrying on business, stalls may
be seen on footpaths selling stolen property and food stuff.

Chinese guerillas are attacking the Japanese forces
at Lingan about 30 miles west of Hangchow and gun fire was
audible at Hangchow.

On the east, certain areas along the motor road to
Shanghai are said to be infested with mobile units from Yuan Hwa. 袁化
Many houses at this Section have been destroyed by artillery
fire and bombs.

5月1日，约250名难民乘船抵达上海。其中包括法租界帮会头目张啸林（Chang Siao Ling）的亲属陈璋桂（Chen Chang Kwei）。据这些抵达者称，他们在办好必要的通行证后，于约十天前离开杭州。当接近长安（火车站）西北的桐乡（Tong Si，音译）时，他们遭到自称“流动部队”的匪徒袭击。匪徒洗劫了船只，掳走了约70名他们认为属于富裕家庭的乘客，并弄坏了汽艇。在前往上海的途中，他们被日本哨兵拦截搜查十余次。抵达时，这些人几乎身无分文，行李尽失。

西湖上的新新饭店（Sun Sun Hotel）正被用作日军司令部，而其他旅馆则被改为妓院或兵营。

中国游击队正在杭州以西约30英里的临安攻击日军，杭州可听到枪声。

在东面，据说通往上海的公路沿线某些地区充斥着来自袁化（Yuan Hwa，音译）的流动部队。该区域的许多房屋已被炮火和炸弹摧毁。

Subject Japanese Troop Movements and Chinese Guerilla Units
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

（批：See also Report）

The activities of Chinese mobile units and
guerilla bands in the area between Shanghai and Hangchow
and on the Shanghai-Nanking Railway line have inflicted
a good deal of damage to Japanese military communications
recently and fighting has taken place in the Dien San
Lake (澱山湖) area, Chu Ka Koh (朱家角), and not
far from the village of Sungkiang. Casualties on both
sides are believed to have been heavy and it is for this
reason that the Japanese Command have caused the erection
of additional defence works in and around Shanghai.

It is reported that a re-distribution of the
Japanese Forces, both military and naval, has taken place
lately in the neighbourhood of Shanghai, and their
disposition is as follows :-

10,000 Japanese soldiers and 1,000 men belonging to
the Naval Landing Party were transferred from
the Eastern District to places south-west of
Shanghai, Pootung, Nantao, Lunghwa and Zikawei
because of the threat by Chinese soldiers
filtering in from Haining and Hanyih and
joining forces with the guerilla forces.
(Those soldiers are reported to belong to
General Chang Fah Kwei's Army).

5,000 Japanese soldiers and 500 naval landing party
men were transferred to Sungkiang and Chuking
on the Shanghai-Nanking Railway, from Paoshan,
Nantao and Chapei.

Precautionary Measures against Chinese Mobile Units

昨日，在杨树浦、水电路（Shui Tien Road，音译）、屈家桥（Chueh Ka Jiao，音译）、江湾、吴淞、大场和闸北构筑了铁丝网障碍、沙袋堡垒和战壕。白天，路障会打开一个足够宽的口以供交通通行，而晚上则封闭通道并设置哨兵，作为预防措施。

I have previously declared that the clash between
Japan and China has placed Germany residing in China in a
very difficult position. I have also emphasized that Germany's
relations to both these countries are equally cordial and
nothing so far has happened to alter this attitude.

Führer Hitler declared on February 20 that Germany
and the Reich are adopting a really neutral position.

We have no political interests in China; only cultural
and economic ones and we, Germans, are not standing between
two fronts through no fault of ours. The report regarding the
happenings that took place in Tsingtao in December and January
is the best answer to Reuter's reports, which, while they did
not communicate falsehoods, nevertheless, represented them
in a wrong light.

The Germans of Tsingtao especially Herr Ohlwein and
Herr Hess can be proud to have saved the town from destruction.

With regard to events that happened in Nanking great
merit has been earned by the unselfish actions by our comrade
Christian Kroger and our co-national Herr Edward Sperling.

Uninvited, these three men, at great personal risk
of their lives, came to the aid of the poorest Chinese in

Weihaiwei 12th March.

On Sunday evening the 6th March, a Japanese cruiser, two
auxiliaries and two motor schooners arrived in Weihaiwei harbour and
on the morning of the 7th they were joined by two destroyers. It
was obvious that the Japanese meant business this time.

The Chinese commissioner, Capt. Cheng, accompanied by the
local police and a handful of marines left across country in perfect
order and discipline. There was no looting and not a shot was fired.
Japanese 'planes circled the city dropping leaflets exhorting the
people to be calm as their mission was peaceful and advising the
populace that their desire was that they should fly the five barred
flag, and submit quietly.

Shortly after 2 p.m. Japanese landed parties of marines,
about 400 in all. Two hundred at Eastcliff Hotel Beach and a further
200 at Port Edward pier. Visitors to Weihaiwei will remember the
ferry which used to run between the Island and the mainland, she
was commandeered by the Japanese and utilized in landing men.

But beyond seeing a few Japanese pickets and the Rising
Sun and Five barred flags flying, Weihaiwei remains peaceful.

The greatest credit is due to Mr. Burdett the British
Consul and to the assistance rendered by Mr. Donald Clark, in the
negotiations between the Chinese and Japanese; and the peaceful
taking over of this port is due in no small measure to the untiring
efforts of these two gentlemen.

13th March.

Quietness prevailed in this port until the night of the
12th March, when the Chinese police who had marched out with
Commissioner Cheng launched a night attack at 2:00 a.m. on Port
Edward Pier, fighting continued until 2:00 p.m. of the same day.
The Japanese had 450 of their marines engaged supported by air-
craft and artillery. The local ex-police put up a magnificent fight
and withdrew very slowly towards the villages of T'ien Sheng and
Pi Chia T'an where the Japanese broke off the fight.

The members engaged on both sides were approximately the
same, the Chinese force losing approximately 40 men and the Japanese
30, according to reliable sources. Japanese 'planes were up and
bombed the foothills around Port Edward without, however, doing any
appreciable damage.

Conditions are again peaceful to-day but rumours are afoot
of a large scale attack which will be launched in the next few days.

JCSB. From A.C. A.T.R.

威海卫，3月12日。

3月6日星期日晚上，一艘日本巡洋舰、两艘辅助舰和两艘摩托帆船抵达威海卫港，7日上午，又有两艘驱逐舰加入。显然，日本人这次是动真格的。

中国专员郑船长（Capt. Cheng）在当地警察和一小队海军陆战队的陪同下，秩序井然、纪律严明地撤离至乡下。没有发生抢劫，也没有开一枪。日本飞机在城市上空盘旋，投下传单，敦促民众保持冷静，声称其使命是和平的，并建议民众悬挂五色旗，安静顺从。

下午2点后不久，日本海军陆战队登陆部队上岸，总共约400人。两百人在东崖酒店海滩，另外200人在爱德华港码头。去过威海卫的游客会记得那艘曾在岛屿和大陆之间运行的渡轮，它被日军征用并用于运送人员登陆。

但是，除了看到几个日本哨兵以及飘扬的旭日旗和五色旗外，威海卫依然平静。

最大的功劳归于英国领事 Burdett 先生以及 Donald Clark 先生在中日谈判中提供的协助；这个港口的和平接管在很大程度上归功于这两位绅士的不懈努力。

3月13日。

该港口一直保持平静，直到3月12日晚，随郑专员撤出的中国警察在凌晨2:00对爱德华港码头发动了夜间袭击，战斗持续到当天下午2:00。日军投入了450名海军陆战队员，并有飞机和炮兵支援。当地的前警察进行了英勇的战斗，并非常缓慢地向田升（T'ien Sheng）和毕家潭（Pi Chia T'an）村庄撤退，日军在那里停止了战斗。

据可靠消息来源，双方参战人数大致相同，中方损失约40人，日方损失30人。日本飞机出动并轰炸了爱德华港周围的山脚，但未造成明显损害。

今天局势再次恢复平静，但有谣言称将在未来几天内发动大规模进攻。

JCSB. 来自 A.C. A.T.R.
SBR. 3月16日

JAPANESE MAY
CHANGE THEIR
COMMAND HERE

Reports of Gen. Matsui's
Recall Gain Ground

GEN. HATA ARRIVES

Japanese Decline to Make
a Statement

Reports that General Iwane Matsui,
Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese
forces in Central China, with his
headquarters in Shanghai, was about
to be recalled, and that his place was
to be taken by General Shunroku
Hata grew more persistent yesterday,
despite the Japanese official attitude
of refusing to discuss the matter
either one way or the other, or to
make any statement on the subject.
From extremely reliable sources,
the "North-China Daily News"
learned yesterday that General Hata
actually arrived in Shanghai on Fri-
day evening. At the Japanese press
conference, the spokesman said that
they were "unable to answer" ques-
tions concerning rumours that Gen-
eral Hata would relieve General
Matsui of his command, and preferred
not to discuss the subject.
Asked who was the prominent
Japanese who arrived at about 5 p.m.
on Friday, when all streets in the
vicinity were roped off and guards

[图片：General Matsui]

posted, the spokesman said that they
preferred not to answer that question.
The "North-China Daily News" under-
stands that the "prominent Japanese"
was none other than General Hata.
A Trans-Ocean message from Lon-
don yesterday stated that, according
to reports reaching the British capital,
General Matsui had been recalled
from his post and would be returning
to Tokyo "at the end of this week."
United Press reported from Tokyo
that Government circles there said
they were without information on the
reported recall of General Matsui.
An official announcement in Tokyo,
however, stated that certain "trans-
fers and re-adjustments" would be
made in Japanese troops in China and
that additional men would be sent to
China to cope with prolonged
hostilities.

The Two Generals
General Matsui has been in com-
mand of the Japanese forces in this
area ever since the beginning of the
hostilities. Although he has made
several secret trips to various parts
of the local sector, his permanent
headquarters is said to be in Shang-
hai. It was under General Matsui's
orders that the so-called "Victory
March" or "transfer of troops" was
carried out some weeks ago through
the International Settlement.
General Hata was only promoted
to his present rank about three
months ago, and up to quite recently
was Commander of the Taiwan
(Formosa) Army. He graduated from
the Military Academy in 1901, and
since then has been Department Chief
of General Staff Office; Commander
of the 5th Field Artillery Brigade;
Chief of the 4th Department, General
Staff Office; Chief of the 1st Depart-
ment in the same office; Inspector of
Artillery; Commander of the 14th
Division; and Chief of the Military
Department of Air, to which he was
appointed in November, 1935.

的传闻甚嚣尘上

畑将军抵达

日军拒绝发表
声明

尽管日本官方持拒绝讨论此事或就此发表任何声明的态度，但关于华中日军总司令、总部设在上海的松井石根（Iwane Matsui）将军即将被召回，并由畑俊六（Shunroku Hata）将军接替其职位的传闻昨日愈发强烈。
《字林西报》昨日从极其可靠的渠道获悉，畑将军实际上已于周五晚上抵达上海。在日本记者招待会上，发言人表示他们“无法回答”有关畑将军将接替松井将军指挥权的传闻的问题，并表示不愿讨论该话题。
当被问及周五下午5点左右抵达的那位显要日本人是谁时——当时附近所有街道都被封锁并部署了警卫——

[图片：松井将军]

发言人表示他们不愿回答这个问题。
《字林西报》了解到，这位“显要日本人”正是畑将军。
昨天来自伦敦的一条跨洋消息称，根据传至英国首都的报告，松井将军已被召回，并将于“本周末”返回东京。
合众社从东京报道说，日本政府圈内人士称他们对有关松井将军被召回的报道一无所知。
然而，东京的一份官方公告指出，将对在华日军进行某些“调动和重新调整”，并将增派人员前往中国以应对持久的敌对行动。

两位将军
自敌对行动开始以来，松井将军一直指挥该地区的日军。虽然他多次秘密前往当地防区的各个部分，但据说他的永久总部设在上海。几周前通过国际租界的所谓“胜利游行”或“部队转移”就是在松井将军的命令下进行的。
畑将军仅在大约三个月前晋升为目前的军衔，直到最近一直是台湾（福尔摩沙）军司令。他于1901年毕业于陆军士官学校，此后历任参谋本部部长；野战炮兵第5旅旅长；参谋本部第四部部长；同一办公室的第一部部长；炮兵总监；第14师团师长；以及航空本部部长，他于1935年11月被任命为该职。

pages.en:
Conqueror Of Yangtze To Depart

General Iwane Matsui, "Little Napoleon"
of the Japanese Army in the Yangtze area,
will turn over his command to General Shun-
roku Hata soon, foreign news agencies report-
ed yesterday. After six world-shaking historic
months, General Matsui will return to Tokyo
for a new assignment. He was scheduled to
leave after the fall of Nanking as that com-
pleted his military task. The Panay, Ladybird
and other incidents delayed the change in
commands, it is believed. His successor is an
Inspector-General of Military Education and
a High Military Counsellor. Born in July,
1879, he was graduated from the Military
Academy in 1901. He has been chief secre-
tary to the General Staff; Commander of the
4th Field Artillery Brigade; Chief 4th De-
partment General Staff Office and also filled
the same office with the 1st Department. He
was an Artillery Inspector, a Commander of
the 14th Division in 1933 and Chief of the
Army Air Service Department.

长江征服者即将离任

据外国新闻机构昨日报道，被称为日军在长江地区“小拿破仑”的松井石根大将，即将把指挥权移交给畑俊六将军。经过六个月震撼世界的历史性时期后，松井大将将返回东京接受新任命。据信，他原定于南京陷落后离职，因为那标志着其军事任务的完成。“帕奈号”、“瓢虫号”及其他事件延误了指挥权的交接。他的继任者是军事教育总监及高级军事顾问。他生于1879年7月，1901年毕业于陆军士官学校。他曾担任参谋本部首席秘书、野战炮兵第四旅团旅团长、参谋本部第四部部长，并曾在第一部担任相同职务。他曾任炮兵监、1933年任第十四师团师团长，以及陆军航空兵部部长。

pages.en:
Situation in the border areas of Kiangsu,
Chekiang and Anhwei Provinces

After a lengthy period of chaos following
the Sino-Japanese hostilities, the border areas of
the three provinces of Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei
have practically returned to normalcy and those
inhabitants fortunate enough to survive the hostilities,
have again settled in their former abodes. The
districts of Ishing (宜興), Li-Yang (溧陽),
Kwangteh (廣德) and Chang Shing (長興) on the
borders of the above mentioned provinces are still
under the control of authorities owing allegiance to
the National Government. Administrative functions
have been carried on for some time past and government
efforts directed at the pacification of the war-stricken
areas are in progress. In order to prevent
undesirable elements from entering the areas, the pre-
war "Pao-Cha" system (a system of mutual guarantee) is
being enforced through various district and village
guilds and inhabitants are required to apply for "good
citizens' certificates" to prove their bona fides when
called upon to do so. Should they fail to produce
such certificates, they are liable to detention by the
district magistrate pending an official investigation.
National Government armed forces operating
or garrisoned in these districts consist of three full
central divisions, namely the 62nd, 73rd and the 108th
Divisions and also the 33rd Independent Brigade,
totalling 35,000 strong, equipped with light guns,
machine guns and rifles. They are active in the
mountainous regions on the border areas, especially in
the vicinity of Ishing and Li-yang.
pages.zh:
江苏、浙江和安徽三省边境地区局势

在中日敌对行动之后经历了长期的混乱，江苏、浙江和安徽三省的边境地区已基本恢复正常，那些幸运地在敌对行动中幸存下来的居民已重新定居在他们原来的住所。上述各省边境上的宜兴、溧阳、广德和长兴地区仍受效忠于国民政府的当局控制。行政职能已在过去一段时间内得以行使，旨在平定战乱地区的政府工作正在进行中。为了防止不良分子进入该地区，战前的“保查”制度（一种互保制度）正通过各区乡公会强制执行，居民在被要求时必须申请“良民证”以证明其身份属实。若未能出示此类证件，他们将面临由区治安官拘留以待官方调查的风险。
在这些地区作战或驻防的国民政府武装部队包括三个完整的中央师，即第六十二师、第七十三师和第一〇八师，以及第三十三独立旅，总兵力达35,000人，装备有轻型火炮、机枪和步枪。他们在边境地区的山区活动频繁，特别是在宜兴和溧阳附近。

pages.en:
- 2 -

The field headquarters of these regular
units of the Chinese National Army are located
somewhere in the Liyang District and in the Tsang
Tse San (張山) in the Ishing District. Un-
interrupted communications are being maintained
between those bases and the Headquarters of the
Chinese High Command.

Observation has revealed that strict
disciplinary rules are being observed among the
Central regular armies, which has gained for them
the support of local inhabitants. Recently,
copies of a circular were posted in Ishing in the
name of General Koo Cheng-lun (谷正倫), Commanding
Officer of the Central Gendarmerie, calling for
applicants desirous of entering the service of the
Central Gendarmerie. Recruits it is said, will
be sent to Hunan for training.

Apart from the Chinese regular units afore-
said, there are guerilla bands which have now been
reorganized into numerous mobile units under the
independent title of "Loyal and Righteous National
Salvation Army" (忠義救國軍), with a total
strength of approximately 50,000 men under the command
of one named Mei (梅).

In the Japanese occupied areas, it appears
that the number of Japanese troops is far from adequate.
Only a few hundred are deployed along the Ishing-Wusieh
Highway, and some 500 garrisoned in the walled city of
Ishing. These troops remain behind strong defence
works and are said to maintain underground communication
with military posts along the Ishing-Wusieh Highway.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

这些中国国民革命军正规部队的野战司令部位于溧阳地区某处以及宜兴地区的张山（Tsang Tse San，音译）。这些基地与中国最高统帅部之间保持着不间断的通讯联络。

观察显示，中央正规军严格遵守纪律规定，这为他们赢得了当地居民的支持。最近，以中央宪兵司令谷正伦将军的名义在宜兴张贴了通告副本，招募希望加入中央宪兵服役的人员。据说，新兵将被送往湖南受训。

除了上述中国正规部队外，还有一些游击队，现已重组为众多机动部队，独立番号为“忠义救国军”，在一位姓梅（Mei，音译）的人指挥下，总兵力约50,000人。

在日军占领区，日军兵力似乎远远不足。仅有数百人部署在宜兴-吴锡公路上，另有约500人驻守在宜兴城墙内。这些部队停留在坚固的防御工事后方，据说与沿宜兴-吴锡公路的军事哨所保持地下通讯联络。

pages.en:
- 3 -

In an effort to capture this city, Chinese
regular units have launched several offensives on
the Japanese garrison troops in Ishing but no tangible
results have been achieved, and it has been decided
to leave the city alone. Occasional skirmishes
however, are inadvertent since tax collectors of
the administrative organs under the Reformed Government,
accompanied by small squads of Japanese soldiers,
visit the countryside from time to time to impose
land tax from the villagers in the form of ten catties
of rice for each "mow" of land, no cash being accepted
for payment of tax. Upon receipt of information
regarding the activities of these tax collectors, troops
are detached by the Chinese regular units to effect
their expulsion which inevitably result in a clash
between them.

So far, the Japanese have made no attempt
to launch any attack upon the Chinese positions and
appeared to be quite satisfied with what they have
already obtained and occupied.

In the Japanese occupied areas, inhabitants
are also required to acquire "good residents' certificates".
pages.zh:
- 3 -

为了攻占这座城市，中国正规部队对宜兴的日军守备部队发动了几次进攻，但未取得实质性成果，因此决定不再攻打该城。然而，偶尔会发生小规模冲突，这是因为维新政府行政机构的征税人员在小股日军士兵的陪同下，不时下乡向村民征收土地税，形式为每“亩”土地缴纳十斤大米，不接受现金支付。一旦收到有关这些征税人员活动的情报，中国正规部队便会分兵将其驱逐，这不可避免地导致双方发生冲突。

到目前为止，日军未尝试对中国阵地发动任何攻击，似乎对他们已经获得和占领的东西感到相当满意。

在日军占领区，居民也被要求获取“良民证”。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
S. E. 03645
No. S. B. D.
APR 6 1939

Chiang Orders Closing
Of Booms At Ningpo And
Wenchow Harbour Mouths

Vessels Ordered To Leave Boom Areas, Causing
Considerable Tie-Up In Sailings; Presence
Of Japanese Warships Portends Attack

CIVILIAN POPULATION OF BOTH PORTS
BEING REMOVED, REPORT STATES

The closing of the booms in the Yungkiang River, in Chenhai, near Ningpo, by 5 p.m. yesterday, and the closing of the Oukiang River in Wenchow, by midnight last night, had been ordered by General Chiang Kai-shek, in telegraphic instructions to the Chekiang Chinese military authorities, it was reliably reported in local shipping circles yesterday.

All the steamers plying within the boom areas had been ordered to leave at the specified "deadline."

Since the outbreak of the current hostilities, it was further stated, a small gap had been left open in the two river booms for in-coming and out-going steamers to pass through. It is said that mines have now been laid within the boom areas.

Many local shipping firms with steamers plying between Shanghai and the East Chekiang ports, have suspended their shipping services for the time being, commencing yesterday, following the expected closure of the two river booms.

Populace Leaving

Meanwhile, the populace in Wenchow and in Ningpo are being steadily evacuated under the auspices of the Chekiang Chinese military authorities. No one, whether young or old, male or female, is permitted to lag behind in either of the towns unless his or her presence is absolutely necessary in connection with military defence measures, it was reported yesterday.

Heavy quantities of cargo and foodstuffs, hitherto stored in Ningpo and Wenchow, have been shipped either to Hongkong or Shanghai during the past few days, local shipping circles revealed yesterday.

Although no untoward incident had occurred up till yesterday, the situation in nevertheless felt to be rather tense, as over 20 Japanese warships are reported to be now concentrated in the Hangchow Bay. However, no hostile activities have so far been embarked upon by the Japanese warships, it was further stated.

Highway communication between Kinhwa and Ningpo is still being satisfactorily maintained, contrary to current rumours. Less goods, however, are now being transported along the highway than a few weeks ago, as most Chinese merchants have ceased to order more goods since the fall of Nanchang.

Boat To Be Sunk

According to the latest telegraphic advices received by local Chinese merchants, the situation in Ningpo and Wenchow was still normal and very quiet up till yesterday. Reports that the two towns had been successively raided during the past few days proved to be incorrect, it was revealed.

Chinese telegraphic advices received last night stated that s.s. Lao Taiping, was being held in readiness at the mouth of the Yungkiang River to be sunk at short notice, in order to block the gap in the boom.

蒋介石下令关闭
宁波和温州港口的拦河坝

船只奉命离开拦河坝区域，导致航运严重停滞；日军舰艇的存在预示着攻击

报道称两港平民正在撤离

据当地航运界昨日可靠消息，蒋介石将军已向浙江中国军事当局发出电报指示，下令于昨日下午5时前关闭宁波附近镇海的甬江拦河坝，并于昨晚午夜前关闭温州的瓯江拦河坝。

所有在拦河坝区域内航行的轮船均被命令在规定的“最后期限”前离开。

据进一步称，自当前敌对行动爆发以来，两条河流的拦河坝一直留有一个小缺口，供进出的轮船通过。据说现在拦河坝区域内已布设水雷。

许多拥有往返上海和浙东港口轮船的当地航运公司，鉴于两条河流拦河坝预期关闭，已于昨日起暂时暂停航运服务。

民众撤离

与此同时，在浙江中国军事当局的主持下，温州和宁波的民众正在稳步撤离。据报道，除非其存在对于军事防御措施绝对必要，否则无论老少男女，均不得在这两个城镇中的任何一个滞留。

当地航运界昨日透露，迄今为止储存在宁波和温州的大量货物和食品，在过去几天内已运往香港或上海。

尽管直到昨天尚未发生任何不幸事件，但局势仍被认为相当紧张，因为有报道称20多艘日本军舰目前集中在杭州湾。不过，据进一步称，日本军舰迄今未采取任何敌对行动。

与当前的谣言相反，金华和宁波之间的公路交通仍然保持良好。然而，现在通过公路运输的货物比几周前少，因为自南昌陷落以来，大多数中国商人已停止订购更多货物。

船只将被沉没

根据当地中国商人收到的最新电报消息，直到昨天，宁波和温州的局势仍然正常且非常平静。此前几天两镇相继遭到袭击的报道被证实是不实的。

昨晚收到的中文电报称，“老太平”轮正停泊在甬江口待命，以便在短时间内将其沉没，从而堵塞拦河坝的缺口。

Chinghai Closed
To Shipping
Gen. Chiang's Orders to
Meet Japanese Threat;
Boom Ship Prepared

Because of the tense military
situation existing along the east
Chekiang coast, Chinghai, important
riverport gateway to Ningpo, the
most important commercial trade
centre in Chekiang on which Shang-
hai depends for the supply of many
goods will be indefinitely and com-
pletely closed to shipping commenc-
ing to-day, according to information
received by shipping circles in
Shanghai.

The closing of the port has been
ordered by General Chiang Kai-
shek and it took effect last night
when the ss. Taiping especially
prepared for erecting a boom was to
be used. Three Shanghai foreign-
owned steamers including a German
boat, which were anchored off
Chinghai were to sail to Shanghai
yesterday afternoon and many other
Shanghai steamers have indefinitely
postponed their trips to the Chekiang
port.

Chinhai, it will be recalled, was
partially closed to shipping many
months ago for military reasons.
Chinese authorities were considerate,
however, since the port has im-
portant business connections with
Shanghai. An opening was left for
boats to proceed to the port but the
threatened large-scale attacks by the
Japanese forces has apparently
caused the Chinese high command
to make the last decision.

The other important Chekiang
district now still open to Shanghai
shipping is Wenchow. The opinion
was freely expressed in shipping
circles yesterday that it might also
be completely closed and if it is
closed then Shanghai will be en-
tirely cut off from Chekiang as far
as shipping business is concerned.

Recently Chinese military authori-
ties have been engaged in helping
Chinese civilians to evacuate from
Ningpo and Wenchow presumably
in preparation for the closing of the
districts. Since the occupation of
Nanchang by Japanese forces, goods
from the interior destined for Shang-
hai and Hongkong have been piled
up in the two Chekiang districts but
it is learnt that during the past few
days the local authorities have done
their best to have them transported
to their destinations.

Attempt to Cross Chientang River

The Japanese forces in Hangchow
have made another futile attempt to
cross the Chientang River in order
to attack the Chinese forces stationed
on the southern bank of the river
and indicating their strong deter-
mination in attacking east Chekiang
24 war vessels are anchored along
the coast now instead of only a few.
Planes have been sent up but no
bombs dropped.

The attempt, according to Chinese
reports, was made on Sunday last
when more than 500 Japanese
soldiers tried to cross the river
under cover of artillery fire. It was
claimed that the Chinese forces put
up strong resistance and that the
Japanese were driven back.

《字林西报》，
033.9

镇海对航运关闭
蒋介石将军为应对日本威胁下达命令；阻塞船已准备就绪

据上海航运界收到的消息，由于浙江东部沿海存在紧张的军事局势，镇海——作为宁波的重要河港门户，而宁波是浙江最重要的商业中心，上海依赖其供应许多货物——将从今天起无限期地完全禁止航运。

港口的关闭是由蒋介石将军下令的，并于昨晚生效，当时专门用于设置阻塞线的“太平”号轮船（ss. Taiping）被投入使用。三艘停泊在镇海外的上海外籍轮船，其中包括一艘德国船只，原定于昨天下午驶往上海，而许多其他上海轮船已无限期推迟前往该浙江港口的行程。

回想起来，镇海早在数月前就曾因军事原因部分关闭航运。然而，鉴于该港口与上海有着重要的商业联系，中国当局此前一直予以关照。虽然曾留出一个通道供船只进入该港口，但日军大规模进攻的威胁显然促使中国最高指挥部做出了最终决定。

目前仍对上海航运开放的另一个重要浙江地区是温州。昨日航运界普遍表示，温州也可能被完全关闭，如果一旦关闭，那么在航运业务方面，上海将与浙江完全隔绝。

最近，中国军事当局一直在帮助中国平民从宁波和温州撤离，这大概是为关闭这些地区做准备。自从日军占领南昌以来，原本运往上海和香港的中国内地货物堆积在这两个浙江地区，但据悉在过去几天里，地方当局已尽力将这些货物运往目的地。

试图渡过钱塘江

驻杭州的日军再次徒劳地试图渡过钱塘江，以攻击驻扎在江南岸的中国军队，这表明了他们进攻浙江东部的强烈决心。目前沿岸停泊的军舰多达24艘，而此前仅有几艘。飞机已升空，但未投掷炸弹。

据中方报告，此次尝试发生于上周日，当时500多名日军士兵在炮火掩护下试图渡河。据称，中国军队进行了顽强抵抗，并将日军击退。

that, the "New Fourth Army", a Communist army, is a new force
recently dispatched by the Nationalist Government to this
part of China and, owing to its special training and experience
in guerilla warfare, it will, it is confidently expected, play
an important part in the Sino-Japanese conflicts in the

had a force of approximately 100,000 men. The order for a
general mobilization of the army was issued immediately

Subject Conditions between Shanghai and Hangchow.

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by C Crawford D.D.

The following information has been obtained from a
source that, in the past, has proved reliable:-

At present the Japanese Telegraph Office despatches
daily an armed convoy of trucks laden with mail matter,
documents, reports, supplies, etc. to Hangchow from Shanghai.
The trucks are invariably driven by non-Japanese foreigners
or Eurasians, who have an extensive knowledge of the
Japanese language. The informer, who drives one of these
trucks, states that during recent trips to and from
Hangchow, which are made via the Hangchow Highway and which
take four hours in each direction, considerable numbers of
Chinese plain clothes' snipers are to be observed en route.
These men, who all appear to be well armed, invariably fire
on the passing convoys, and in some spots on the road where
the cover of dense undergrowth permits, attempt to ambush

From a reliable source it is learned that fifteen
multiple engined Soviet Bombers, operating from a secret base
situated between Hankow and Canton raided Formosa approximately
one week ago. Only Soviet personnel took part in the raid.

agency has been established in Sydney, Australia, to facilitate
the enlistment of mechanics and pilots for the Chinese Air
Force. Preference is given to men who have had previous
flying experience and preferential treatment is given to
applicants who are able to prove that they held short service
commissions in the Royal Air Force. A bonus is paid to accepted
candidates who sail by the first available boat from Sydney
to Hongkong. It is reported that a number of recruits have

It has been learned from a reliable source that
the Chinese troops have placed four mines in the sewers on
Boundary Road three yards North of the Boundary gates and
"B" Blockhouse. All four mines are connected by electric
wire and are under one control switch located in the sand-
bag emplacement situated in Chinese territory some distance
North of the Boundary gates. The top of an ordinary garbage
bin marks the spot where the mines are hidden. It is
believed that the Chinese Military Authorities have assured
the British Military Authorities that the mines were placed as
a safeguard against a possible Japanese attack in that sector,
and that the British Authorities would be given due notice
should it become necessary to fire the mines. It has not
been ascertained whether the Chinese expect the Japanese to
attack from the North (Chinese territory) or the South
(Settlement) but in this connection it is pointed out that
the mines are so placed that they could not possibly check
a Japanese advance from Chinese territory via Jukong, Hongshing,
Paotung, Paochang or Kongshing Roads as the mines are south
of these arteries. They can, therefore, have only one
significance - to destroy the gates (a) in the event of the
Chinese troops forcing an entry into the Settlement at this
point with the object of launching an attack on the Japanese
in the Hongkew area or (b) as a means of checking any Japanese
advance from the Settlement end should the Japanese succeed
in opening or forcing the gates.
It has also been ascertained that there are 6,000
Honanese troops in the vicinity of the North Railway Station.

事由 中国军队在界门以北等地埋设地雷。
撰写人 副督察长劳里尔（D.S.I. Laurier） 转呈人 首席督察克劳福德（C. Crawford, D. I.）

据可靠消息来源获悉，中国军队已在界路（Boundary Road）下水道内、界门及“B”号碉堡以北三码处埋设了四枚地雷。这四枚地雷均通过电线连接，由一个控制开关统一操控，该开关位于界门以北一段距离处、处于中国领土内的沙袋工事中。一处普通垃圾桶的顶部标记了地雷隐藏的位置。据悉，中国军方当局已向英国军方当局保证，埋设地雷是为了防范日军在该区域可能发动的袭击，并承诺若确有必要引爆炸药，将提前通知英国当局。目前尚不清楚中方是否预期日军会从北面（中国领土）或南面（租界）发起进攻，但在此需指出，地雷的布置位置决定了它们不可能阻挡日军经由菊恭路（Jukong Road）、鸿兴路（Hongshing Road）、宝通路（Paotung Road）、宝昌路（Paochang Road）或公兴路（Kongshing Road）从中国领土方向推进，因为这些地雷位于上述干道以南。因此，其目的只有一种解释——(a) 在中国军队试图由此处强行进入租界、旨在对虹口地区日军发动攻击的情况下，炸毁界门；或 (b) 一旦日军成功打开或强行突破界门，以此作为阻滞日军从租界一侧推进的手段。

另经查实，北站附近有6,000名河南籍士兵。

The Chinese Officers consist mostly of Cantonese and Honanese.
The Chinese troops in this area are short of food and
ammunition, though it is anticipated that further supplies of
ammunition for the troops in this area are now en route from
Nanking. Many of the Chinese troops are armed with Mauser
(Military type) pistols and each man carries a hand-grenade
in each of his two tunic breast pockets. It is expected that
this area will be quiet tomorrow, 20th instant but on the
21st a large scale offensive is expected to take place.
There are indications that the Chinese troops will try to
force an entrance into the Settlement through the Boundary
Road gates and possibly at Markham Road Bridge, which may
explain the true objective of the mines placed at these two
points.
